text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Some of Zimbabwe's junior doctors and nurses who were fired by the government for defying a call to return to work after going on strike to press for better wages and working conditions are expected to appeal against their dismissals or re-apply for their jobs.
- Crop-planting in most parts of Zimbabwe could soon be underway following light to heavy rains which fell in several areas over the weekend and on Monday.

- A local quality check organisation, Standards Association of Zimbabwe on Monday challenged countries in the Southern African Development Community to take advantage of the stable environment in the region to improve the market competitiveness of their products.
